title: Cannot replace with positive lookbehind including `\n`

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

body:
Type: Bug I cannot replace regex `(?<=\n)b` to "BBB" in this text below: ``` a-b-c a-b-d a-b-e a-c-d a-c-e a-d-e b-c-d b-c-e b-d-e c-d-e ``` Texts can be found like this. ![ss007 - ● a-b-c ？ Untitled-1 - Visual Studio Code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/assets/88940383/1614a4f8-f4c2-45d9-aae7-d1a2e9237abd) But, single replace fails like this. ![ss008 - ● a-b-c ？ Untitled-1 - Visual Studio Code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/assets/88940383/11f6a9c4-25ec-4aa2-8dea-bf7d72098b16) Using literal line break in regexp or using `LF` as line break code also fails. ![ss008 - ● a-b-c ？ Untitled-1 - Visual Studio Code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/assets/88940383/5e4ecbc3-2e92-4b2a-a0a5-efb9b1b55932) This behavior only occurs with single replace. If I use multiple replace (Ctrl+Alt+Enter), the replace works correctly. ![ss004 - ● a-b-c ？ Untitled-1 - Visual Studio Code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/assets/88940383/9c74bc5d-d9a7-4540-8da2-3a389fc58733) This behavior occurs when I use positive lookbehind with `\n`. If I use regexp without `\n` or without positive lookbehind, the replace works correctly. ![ss003 - ● a-b-c ？ Untitled-1 - Visual Studio Code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/assets/88940383/e0762a13-1b09-4cca-a646-dcb4640d1d36) ![ss001 - ● a-BBB-c ？ Untitled-1 - Visual Studio Code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/assets/88940383/0229fa24-5ce8-4d5f-8cad-0aef71f9eb45) ![ss002 - ● a-b-c ？ Untitled-1 - Visual Studio Code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/assets/88940383/62708a5f-5de4-4eac-b13f-60ccd619ca14) ---- I tried insider version with vscode.dev, but replace failed too. title: Find with "Match Whole Word" misses valid occurrences

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

body:
Type: Bug 1. Copy into an empty document the following text: [1] aa-aa [2] xaa-aa-aa [3] aax-aa-aa 2. Use Find (CTRL-F) to find the string aa-aa 3. An instance of the string appear in every line. We can argue if line 2 should have 2 instances but that would be too much of nitpicking. 4. Turn on Match whole-word for Find 5. VScode only shows a match for lines 1 and 3 even though line 2 has a match. grep -w 'aa-aa' on the text would show 3 matches. title: Copy Line Up/Down commands do not preserve more than two multi-cursors on the same line

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->

<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.116.0-insider (user setup)
- OS Version: Windows 11

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Write a line of text, e.g. `foo bar baz`
2. Place at least 3 cursors on the same line from left to right with Alt+Click, e.g. 
   - start with `foo| bar baz`,
   - follow with `foo| bar| baz`,
   - and finally `foo| bar| baz|`
3. Copy that line up or down using Shift+Alt+Up/Down Arrow

Expected: All cursors are moved to the copied line, e.g. with Shift+Alt+Down Arrow,

```
foo bar baz
foo| bar| baz|
```

Actual: Only the first cursor and the leftmost non-first cursor are moved down to the copied line, e.g.

```
foo bar baz
foo| bar| baz
```

Notice how the cursor after `baz` is gone.
